subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: What received-value disclosure contract should human-facing config validation use when source literals differ from effective values or belong to plugin-defined config?
rationale: Choosing between accurate effective values, raw literals, or omission changes both diagnostic truthfulness and the risk of writing credentials into terminals or service logs; repository policy cannot safely infer that product/security boundary.

options.title: Safe effective values
options.body: Use the effective rejected input, but render it only when canonical secret-target metadata proves the path and value non-sensitive; otherwise omit it.

options.title: Raw literals only
options.body: Display only source-file literals with proven locations, accepting that environment and include resolution can make the hint differ from the rejected value.

options.title: Defer value hints
options.body: Land bracket paths and source locations now, and leave received values out until a broader disclosure contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Safe effective values
recommendation.body: Use the effective rejected input, but render it only when canonical secret-target metadata proves the path and value non-sensitive; otherwise omit it.

likelyOwner.reason: The current config CLI and secret-target registry are the nearest available ownership boundary for this decision.
